domains.title: Managed-runtime object models
domains.depth: Mechanism construction, experimental falsification and independent transfer

subtopics.title: Pointer tags, NaN payloads and representation trust boundaries

objectives.text: Derive disjoint number and integer bit partitions, pointer round-trip preconditions and negative decoding; classify portable arithmetic, implementation-defined pointer mapping and explicit IEEE-format assumptions.

Implement numeric NaN canonicalization, int32 boxing/unboxing and checked two-bit pointer tags from the exact contract. Build a discriminated-union alternative and a character-copy double bridge with verified format assumptions; never truncate a pointer into a payload.

Enumerate signed extrema and NaN payload collisions, signed zero, infinities, misaligned integer mappings and reserved bits. Reject missing-canonicalization and sign-loss mutants; compare integer decoding with Python integers and verify native pointer round trips only for admitted live objects.

Change to a capability-pointer target or a binary32-only implementation: derive an explicit handle representation and revise every pointer/NaN assumption. Delayed assessment introduces a serialized attacker-controlled NaN word; demonstrate why decoding it cannot authorize a host pointer.

subtopics.title: Owned binary interning and collision-safe symbol identity

objectives.text: Explain canonical identity versus byte equality, table ownership, embedded-NUL handling and why collisions cannot prove equality. Distinguish strong intern retention from weak symbol tables.

Implement the eight-entry copied-string table with first-insertion IDs and atomic admission failure, then implement a hashed table with explicit collision chains or probing and transactional resizing; compare both on the same byte-string contract.

Generate binary strings including empty, embedded NUL and equal-length different bytes. Inject failure on hits and misses, exhaust capacity and preserve output/state snapshots. Reject length-only equality and ignored-admission-failure mutants; use a Python dictionary as an independent identity oracle.

Replace strong retention with weak interning linked to collector epochs, defining when IDs retire and whether reinterned bytes regain the same identity. Delayed assessment retains a symbol across a moving collection and forces an allocation failure during rehash.

subtopics.title: Immutable hidden classes and reusable property transitions

objectives.text: Derive ordered layout descriptors and transition identity, distinguishing an equal property set from an equal storage layout. State ownership of shapes, receiver fields and transition caches.

Implement immutable four-field shapes in a16-shape arena, transition reuse by parent-plus-key and atomic capacity failure. Add a dictionary-mode alternative for deletion and compare its explicit lookup/invalidation contract.

Construct same-order and permuted-order receivers, update existing properties at full capacity, exhaust transition storage and test rollback. Reject parent-omission and omitted-receiver-transition mutants; independently compare every lookup with a property dictionary.

Add property deletion, attributes and a prototype chain. Derive which operations preserve shape identity and which invalidate caches. Delayed assessment permits shape ID reuse and requires a generation or epoch policy that rejects stale descriptors.

Explain a cached lookup handler versus a cached value, and prove why owner, shape and property key jointly determine this model offset. Bound the cases in which immutable shapes remove invalidation needs.

Implement a two-entry polymorphic cache with monomorphic first state, sticky generic fallback, owner reset and current-receiver field loads. Compare always-generic lookup with the same output and missing-key effects.

Alternate receivers with different insertion orders and property names at one cache, update field values, switch arenas and test missing outputs. Reject missing-shape and missing-key guards; count hits/misses before timing equivalent workloads.

Add prototype-chain access or shape retirement with weak cache references, then design invalidation tokens and deoptimization fallback. Delayed assessment inserts an accessor whose callback mutates the receiver during lookup.

subtopics.title: Incremental marking and root/store write barriers

objectives.text: Derive the no-black-to-white-edge invariant and distinguish incremental mutation between steps from concurrent mutation. Explain floating garbage and why root updates need their own barrier.

Implement begin, bounded scan steps, black-source stores and root insertion for the16-object graph. Build an explicit gray-worklist alternative with a capacity proof, and add immediate quiescent sweeping under a stated allocation policy.

Enumerate small graphs/root sets against graph reachability; stop after blackening a root, then insert a white child and add a new white root. Reject missing-object and missing-root barriers, test budget0, cycles and invalid edges, and account for scan work separately from elapsed time.

Permit allocation during an active cycle and compare black allocation, gray allocation and a restart policy. Delayed assessment replaces serialized mutation with a concurrent mutator; derive publication ordering and termination detection rather than adding volatile.

subtopics.title: Semispace evacuation, forwarding and promotion failure

objectives.text: Derive identity preservation under copying, forwarding uniqueness and the old-to-young root obligation. Explain the empirical generational hypothesis separately from the correctness of a minor collection.

Implement two young semispaces with first-survival aging, second-survival promotion, complete root/edge rewriting and atomic capacity failure. Replace the whole-state transaction copy with a preflight or rollback design while retaining the same failure contract.

Compare surviving payload identities and edge relations against graph reachability over all small graphs. Test cycles, aliases, old-only roots, two successive collections and promotion exhaustion. Reject skipped-old-roots and stale-root-rewrite mutants, measuring copied survivors rather than claiming every allocation is cheap.

Integrate card scanning and a major collector; choose a promotion policy under an adversarial long-lived workload and bounded old capacity. Delayed assessment adds large nonmovable objects and requires a precise pinning/fragmentation policy.

subtopics.title: Card marking and conservative remembered roots

objectives.text: Derive old-to-young completeness and distinguish safe false positives from unsafe false negatives. Explain why overwriting one field cannot clear a card shared by another field.

Implement two-object cards over eight old objects, store marking and dirty-card rescanning with retained young edges. Integrate it with the nursery through an explicit adapter, retaining full-old scanning as an independent reference.

Enumerate object/field/target stores, test two young edges sharing a card, overwrite one and then both, and count exactly four field scans per dirty card. Reject omitted marking and premature clearing mutants; compare survivor graphs with the full-scan nursery.

Add concurrent card scanning with a writer racing card clearing and design an epoch/double-buffer or synchronization protocol. Delayed assessment changes card size and cache-line placement; revise false-positive work and cache traffic measurements.
Distinguish object identity, handle identity and physical slot, and derive when outstanding raw borrows prohibit movement. Explain forwarding for aliased handles and nested handle fields.

Implement stable physical packing of live payloads with old-slot forwarding and updating every handle alias, then add a pinned-object alternative with explicit fragmentation costs and a generation policy for reused handles.

Enumerate all small live masks and compare payload identity through handles before and after movement. Test holes, aliases, cycles through handles, empty/full heaps, and borrow rejection; reject omitted-handle-rewrite and ignored-borrow mutants.

Integrate a pool allocator and a foreign-function API that temporarily exposes raw pointers. Design pin/unpin lifetime and cancellation cleanup, and measure the tradeoff against copying handles. Delayed assessment allows handle-slot reuse with a stale external reference.

subtopics.title: Ephemeron fixed points and staged finalization

objectives.text: Derive conditional reachability of ephemeron values and why a value-to-key cycle cannot bootstrap liveness. Separate weak clearing, finalizer retention, resurrection and deterministic external-resource release.

Implement repeated ephemeron closure, weak clearing before finalizer retention, an explicit pending queue and at-most-once finalization identities. Build a synthetic finalizer driver that may resurrect an object and compare the chosen policy with Lua and CPython.

Enumerate small ephemeron relations/root sets independently, include reverse-ordered chains requiring multiple passes, value-key cycles, weak-only roots, pending-queue rejection and resurrection followed by later reclamation. Reject single-pass and missing-finalized-bit mutants.

Add a finalizer that fails while owning a synthetic resource and one that allocates; specify queue capacity, reentry and eventual cleanup without relying on prompt GC. Delayed assessment changes ephemeron values into graphs containing further ephemeron keys.
Derive residual external counts for a candidate subgraph, then prove why residual zero alone does not imply garbage. Preserve true counts while detecting a candidate reachability closure.

Implement copied trial counts, candidate-internal edge subtraction, rescue from positive residual seeds, and reclamation with decrements to surviving targets. Integrate ordinary zero-count cascading separately and compare with a tracing oracle.

Enumerate three-node graphs, external roots and candidate subsets, including self-cycles, shared descendants, parallel edges, externally protected cycles and inconsistent counts. Reject omitted subtraction and missing rescue closure; verify true survivor counts and exact reclaimed sets.

Add deferred decrements and candidate buffering, bounding pause and memory cost under repeated mutations. Delayed assessment introduces concurrent retain/release and asks which snapshots and synchronization are needed before a trial result can justify reclamation.

subtopics.title: Precise root maps and derived-reference relocation

objectives.text: Derive complete root maps over initialized interpreter slots, distinguishing scalar lookalikes, duplicate copies and derived base-plus-offset references. Explain compiler statepoints versus manually maintained C roots.

Implement transactional map validation and relocation of every root copy, preserving scalar slots and one-past offsets. Integrate actual runtime.vm roots and temporaries through ADAPTERS.md, then construct and inspect an LLVM statepoint experiment as a separate compiler-dependent artifact.

Enumerate base/destination/offset combinations, exact maps, missing roots, uninitialized slots, missing forwarding and non-safepoint rejection. Reject omitted-map-validation and omitted-relocation mutants; inspect pre/post values and demonstrate why stale hidden compiler copies require compiler cooperation.

Add multiple interpreter frames, exceptions and foreign calls that can allocate. Design root registration/unregistration on every exit and safepoint poll protocol. Delayed assessment moves an object while two derived references and a scalar with equal bits are live.
